idea_name: Diagnosing Where Global Boundary Models Fail on SEA Smallholdings
bucket: 5 - field / parcel boundary and sub-field structure
one_sentence_pitch: For agricultural extension agronomists supporting smallholder farmers in Vietnam and Cambodia, we run a stratified diagnosis of exactly which landscape conditions (field size, slope, tree-canopy overlap, fragmentation) break the zero-shot global field-boundary model Delineate Anything v2, then fix the single dominant failure mode with a terrain/canopy-conditioned adapter and measure the gain specifically on the strata where the global model fails.
problem_statement: Global field-delineation foundation models now report strong aggregate zero-shot accuracy across 61-100 countries (Delineate Anything v2, arXiv:2607.19069), but country- or continent-level aggregates hide stratum-specific collapse: sub-0.5ha plots, sloped/terraced terrain, and tree-crop/agroforestry canopy overlap are known to break flat-farmland-trained boundary models (as GTPBD/GTPBD-MM, arXiv:2507.14697 and arXiv:2604.12315, showed for terraced parcels generally). Southeast Asian smallholdings combine several of these hard conditions simultaneously, yet no published evaluation decomposes performance by these strata for SEA specifically, and no fix has been validated against the specific mechanism that breaks the model there (as opposed to a general fine-tune-on-local-data gain). Extension agronomists therefore have no evidence-based way to know whether a deployed global model's outputs can be trusted on a given smallholder plot, or why it fails when it does.
proposed_technical_approach: (1) Build a stratified SEA smallholder evaluation set from AI4SmallFarms (Vietnam and Cambodia, 439,001 manually digitised field polygons, IEEE GRSL 2023), tagging every tile with: field-size quartile (from the polygons themselves), slope/aspect bucket (from Copernicus DEM GLO-30), tree-canopy-cover fraction bucket (from ESA WorldCover 10m tree-cover class as a canopy-overlap proxy), and a fragmentation index (parcel density per km^2). (2) Run Delineate Anything v2 zero-shot (frozen, pretrained weights) on every tile and compute per-tile instance-segmentation metrics (mAP@0.5, boundary IoU, object-F1); decompose variance in per-tile performance across the four stratum axes (e.g. gradient-boosted feature importance / ANOVA) to identify which axis is the dominant, statistically significant driver of failure. (3) Implement a targeted architectural fix for the dominant axis only: most plausibly a terrain-aware adapter (slope/aspect as an auxiliary input channel fused into the frozen backbone via a lightweight cross-attention adapter, following the DEM-conditioning recipe validated by GTPBD-MM's ETTerra for terraced parcels) or, if canopy closure dominates, a WorldCover tree-cover channel plus an auxiliary canopy-decontamination loss that discourages merging adjacent under-canopy parcels into one instance. (4) Fine-tune only the adapter and decoder head (backbone frozen) on a small labelled SEA subset; evaluate the fix specifically on the failing stratum against two controls: the frozen zero-shot baseline, and a naive full fine-tune on the same SEA subset with no terrain/canopy conditioning at all (this ablation isolates whether any gain is due to the specific conditioning mechanism or is simply generic domain adaptation from seeing local data).

Risk, stated plainly: AI4SmallFarms' actual footprint (Mekong-delta-adjacent Vietnam and Cambodia) may not contain much genuine terracing or dense agroforestry canopy overlap -- if so, the terrain/canopy strata this candidate needs to diagnose may have insufficient variance in the available labelled data, and a supplementary small hand-digitised set (e.g. over Philippine or Indonesian terraces) would be needed, which is itself a real, unbudgeted labelling task.

evaluation_protocol: Per-stratum instance-segmentation metrics (mAP@0.5, boundary IoU, object-F1) computed on held-out AI4SmallFarms tiles, broken out by field-size quartile, DEM-slope bucket, WorldCover tree-cover-fraction bucket, and parcel-density (fragmentation) bucket. Statistical test: ANOVA or gradient-boosted feature-importance across the four stratum axes on per-tile zero-shot performance, to identify which axis explains the most variance (the 'dominant failure mode'). Success criterion: a paired, per-tile, statistically significant IoU/F1 gain on the worst-performing stratum after the targeted terrain/canopy fix, over both (a) the frozen Delineate Anything v2 baseline and (b) a naive-fine-tune-with-no-conditioning ablation on the same SEA subset -- the second comparison is essential to prove the gain comes from the specific mechanism diagnosed, not merely from local fine-tuning.
novelty_delta: The defensible delta, if it holds, is the causal mechanism diagnosis (which specific stratum -- size, slope, canopy, fragmentation -- actually drives failure, isolated by ablation against naive fine-tuning) combined with a measured, stratum-targeted gain over the frozen global SOTA. This is explicitly not 'applied X to Y country': the deliverable is a falsifiable, quantified failure mechanism plus an architectural fix validated against a domain-adaptation confound, not a re-run of an existing pipeline on new geography. However, this delta must be stated honestly as narrow and time-sensitive: as of this research pass, at least three adjacent 2024-2026 papers have already closed parts of the failure space this candidate targets -- 'Fields of the Planet' (arXiv:2607.04449) already fixes the small-field/fragmentation failure mode via higher-resolution (3m PlanetScope) imagery rather than terrain/canopy conditioning; PTAViT3D-CA (arXiv:2409.13568) already validates cross-region transfer including on AI4SmallFarms itself using SAR+optical fusion to address cloud contamination, a major real SEA confound; and GTPBD-MM/ETTerra (arXiv:2604.12315) already validates DEM+text conditioning for terraced parcels, just not for SEA or for canopy overlap specifically. The remaining defensible novel territory is narrow: canopy-closure/agroforestry-specific conditioning combined with SEA smallholder terrain, which as far as this research could confirm has not yet been done -- but this gap could close within months given the publication cadence of the FTW and Delineate Anything research groups.
prior_art_that_threatens_it: Delineate Anything v2 (arXiv:2607.19069) itself already reports a 100-country zero-shot benchmark, though at country-aggregate, not stratum, granularity. 'The first global agricultural field boundary map at 10m resolution' (arXiv:2605.11055, May 2026) already flags over-fragmentation in smallholder systems as a known, named, unresolved failure mode -- meaning the fragmentation half of this candidate's diagnosis is not new. 'Fields of the Planet' (arXiv:2607.04449, July 2026) already demonstrates that the small-field/fragmentation failure is substantially fixed by higher-resolution imagery (PQ on sub-0.5ha fields rising from 5.8 to 15.7 at 3m vs 10m), which directly undercuts a 'fragmentation is the dominant, terrain/canopy-fixable failure mode' framing if fragmentation turns out to dominate in week 1's diagnosis. PTAViT3D-CA (arXiv:2409.13568, tested explicitly on AI4SmallFarms) already shows SAR+optical fusion resolves cloud-contamination-driven failures across smallholder regions including this candidate's own target dataset. GTPBD-MM/ETTerra (arXiv:2604.12315, April 2026) already validates the DEM-conditioning recipe this candidate proposes to reuse, for terraced (though non-SEA) parcels. PRUE (arXiv:2603.27101, March 2026) already runs a systematic 18-model evaluation of segmentation and geospatial foundation models on the FTW benchmark for robustness under real-world conditions, partially closing the 'systematic stratified diagnosis' novelty space, though not with SEA/canopy-specific strata. Taken together, this is an unusually dense cluster of directly adjacent 2024-2026 work from a small number of active groups (the Microsoft/ASU Fields-of-The-World team; the Lavreniuk/Kussul Delineate Anything team; the GTPBD/GTPBD-MM team), each shipping roughly every 1-2 months in 2026.
h2_generic_check: On its face the core is not one of the eight banned H2 patterns (not a chatbot, dashboard, leaf-disease classifier, NDVI viewer, tabular yield model, crop-type-classification rerun, or API-wrapper app). However, the brief itself flags this candidate as the highest genericity risk in the batch, and that flag is justified: the one-sentence template -- 'a global model underperforms in region Y because of local condition X, so we fine-tuned it with X as an extra input' -- is a pattern that could equally describe dozens of other remote-sensing FYPs (flood mapping, building-footprint extraction, land-cover classification, all adapted from a global model to a local condition). This candidate only clears H2 if the diagnosed mechanism is genuinely causal and falsifiable (e.g. a specific, testable claim such as 'overlapping tree crowns cause the instance-segmentation head to merge adjacent parcel masks, verifiable by visual inspection of merged-instance error cases and by an ablation that removes canopy overlap synthetically') rather than a generic 'accuracy went up after we added more local data and an extra channel' result. Verdict: marginal pass, conditional on the mechanism claim being rigorously causal, not merely correlational.
user_segment: Agricultural extension agronomists and smallholder-support cooperatives operating in Vietnam and Cambodia (matching AI4SmallFarms' actual coverage), who use field-boundary maps for parcel-level crop registration, targeted input-subsidy allocation, or (for tree-crop plots) deforestation/EUDR-style traceability checks. Extension to other SEA smallholder contexts (e.g. Malaysian or Indonesian oil-palm/cocoa smallholdings with heavier canopy overlap) is plausible but not currently backed by a verified labelled dataset in this research pass -- stated as a limitation, not a claim.
quantified_pain: Delineate Anything Flow (arXiv:2511.13417) itself quantifies the scale of boundary-completeness failure in a fragmented/smallholder-adjacent system: for Ukraine, its improved pipeline delineated 3.75M fields (at 5m) versus 2.66M from an operational Sinergise Solutions product and 1.69M from NASA Harvest -- a roughly 40-120% undercount by less-tuned pipelines when field fragmentation is high, illustrating the practical scale of the problem this candidate targets, though Ukraine is not itself an SEA smallholder analogue and this number is used only as an illustrative proxy for what boundary-completeness failure costs at scale. [uncertain] A specific, sourced number for the hectares or percentage of Vietnamese/Cambodian smallholder cropland affected by canopy overlap or terracing specifically, or the direct cost to extension agronomists of unreliable global-model boundary outputs, was not found in the sources reviewed and would need primary quantification (e.g. from FAO or national agricultural statistics) in week 1.

An optional extension using commercial-grade PlanetScope/NICFI tropical-forest imagery for supplementary canopy-overlap examples was considered but is not required and its free-tier access route was not independently verified in this pass -- flagged as skippable, budget RM0 if omitted.
demo_artifact: A laptop demo showing one SEA tile: frozen Delineate Anything v2 boundary predictions overlaid on the Sentinel-2 image (visibly merged/broken instances in the high-canopy-overlap or high-slope zone of the tile), side by side with the fixed model's predictions on the same tile, plus a bar chart of per-stratum IoU before and after the fix. Runs in under 2 minutes on pre-cached tiles and pre-trained weights.
build_vs_research_ratio: Approximately 60:40 engineering:research. Engineering: the DEM/WorldCover-to-tile stratification pipeline, the per-stratum metrics computation, and the adapter fine-tuning pipeline plus demo app. Research: the mechanism diagnosis itself, designing the ablation that separates 'the specific conditioning helped' from 'any local fine-tuning helps', and honestly positioning the work against the unusually dense adjacent 2024-2026 literature.
publication_venue_fit: CVPR EarthVision or IGARSS workshop paper -- failure-mode/robustness-diagnosis papers with a targeted fix fit these venues well. Remote Sensing (MDPI) is a realistic fallback given the applied SEA agriculture framing.
key_risks: Data-sufficiency risk: AI4SmallFarms' actual footprint (Mekong-delta-adjacent Vietnam/Cambodia) may not contain enough genuine terracing or dense canopy-overlap variance to support the stratified diagnosis the pitch assumes -- if strata don't vary meaningfully, the core premise collapses and would require supplementary hand-digitised data (an unbudgeted labelling task).

Novelty-erosion risk: the Fields-of-The-World and Delineate Anything research clusters are each shipping roughly one new closely-adjacent paper per 1-2 months through 2026 (Fields of the Planet, PRUE, the global 10m map, GTPBD-MM); a real probability that the exact SEA canopy/terrain diagnosis appears from one of these groups before this project concludes.

Mechanism/causality risk: 'accuracy dropped because of X' claims are easy to assert and hard to prove causally when resolution, terrain, canopy, and cloud cover are correlated in real SEA imagery -- a weak, correlational mechanism claim would tip this candidate into the exact H1/H2 genericity failure the brief warns against.
Statistical-power risk: AI4SmallFarms covers only two countries and 62 tiles, limiting the power of a four-axis stratified ANOVA; conclusions may not generalise even within SEA.

Confound risk: any measured gain from the targeted fix could simply be domain-adaptation-from-seeing-local-data rather than the specific terrain/canopy conditioning mechanism -- this is exactly what the naive-fine-tune ablation is designed to test, and if that ablation shows no meaningful difference, the entire novelty claim fails.
kill_criteria: Week 1-2: (1) Run frozen Delineate Anything v2 zero-shot on AI4SmallFarms test tiles and compute the four-axis stratified breakdown immediately; if performance does not vary meaningfully across DEM-slope and WorldCover tree-cover buckets (i.e. failure is uniform, or dominated by an axis such as resolution or cloud cover that adjacent papers have already fixed), the core premise is false and the project should pivot or stop. (2) Explicitly check whether AI4SmallFarms' actual footprint contains sufficient slope/canopy variance to stratify at all; if the region is essentially flat and canopy-sparse, either widen to a supplementary hand-labelled region in week 1 or abandon. (3) Set a standing arXiv watch on the FTW and Delineate Anything author groups; if a canopy/terrain-conditioned SEA-specific model is published during the project, pivot the delta immediately or reframe as an independent replication with a different, narrower angle.

hard_constraint_verdict.H1: WEAK/CONDITIONAL PASS -- genuine novelty exists only if the week-1 diagnosis confirms a real, unaddressed, and causally demonstrable canopy/terrain-driven failure mode specific to SEA; given the density of adjacent 2024-2026 fixes for fragmentation, cloud cover, and generic terrain, this is the more fragile of the two candidates on H1.
hard_constraint_verdict.H2: MARGINAL PASS -- not a literally banned pattern, but structurally close to the 'apply global model X, find it fails in region Y, fine-tune' genericity trap the brief explicitly names; only cleared if the mechanism diagnosis is rigorously causal.
hard_constraint_verdict.H3: PASS -- Sentinel-2 is the primary imagery input; DEM and WorldCover auxiliary channels, resolutions, revisit, and licences all stated.
hard_constraint_verdict.H4: PASS -- Vietnamese/Cambodian smallholder-support agronomists and co-ops are named; SEA is an explicitly acceptable geography per H4 even without a Singapore-specific angle.
hard_constraint_verdict.H5: PASS -- dataset size (<20GB), compute (a few hours, fits in 24GB), and cash cost (~RM0) are all comfortably within budget.
hard_constraint_verdict.H6: PASS -- a visual before/after boundary-overlay demo with a per-stratum bar chart is a strong, clear 60-second story for a panel.

overall_recommendation: WEAK. The imagery/geography/budget/pitch gates all pass cleanly, but the H1 novelty case is genuinely fragile: the specific failure mode this candidate needs to discover and fix is being actively and rapidly picked apart by several adjacent 2024-2026 papers from a small number of highly active research groups, and the flagship SEA dataset (AI4SmallFarms) may not even contain the terrain/canopy variance the pitch's framing assumes. This candidate should proceed only if the week-1 kill-criteria confirm a real, causally demonstrable, stratum-specific failure with sufficient variance in the available data; absent that confirmation, it risks collapsing into exactly the generic 'applied X to Y region' pattern the brief flags it for.
confidence: Medium. Would rise to High after (a) actually running the frozen Delineate Anything v2 model on AI4SmallFarms and computing the stratified breakdown -- this is precisely the week-1 kill-criteria check and would immediately confirm or refute the premise -- and (b) reading GTPBD-MM's full method and results sections (not just the abstract) to confirm whether its geographic coverage or ablations already extend to SEA-like canopy-overlap conditions.
